words.note: Use هذا for a male and هذه for a female. Groups of things (signs, mountains, books) often take the female word too — the same split as الذي and التي.

words.english: she who, those who (for broken plural)

words.note: A letter (or a few letters) stuck on the end of a word can mean his, her, your, my, our, or their. These are not separate words. كِتَابُهُ = his book.
Not a standalone word - it attaches to the end of a noun (or verb).

A tiny أَ or هَل at the start turns a sentence into a question. أَ sticks to the next word: أَلَمْ = “did not…?”

words.english: than the one who, from those who (م)

words.note: Attaches to the front of the next word, with no space.
The word مَا (“what / that which”) often sticks to the word before it, with no space. بِ + مَا = بِمَا “with what”.
The letters وَ (and), فَ (then), لِ (for/to), بِ (with/in), and كَ (like) attach to the front of the next word, with no space. وَاللَّهُ is “and Allah”, not two words.
Attaches to the front of the next word, with no space. بِهِ = with him / with it.
Attaches to the front of the next word, with no space. كَذَٰلِكَ = like that.
Attaches to the front of the next word, with no space. لَهُ = for him / for it.
A particle of oath, attached to the following word.
Attaches to the front of the next word, with no space. وَاللَّهُ = and Allah.
A letter stuck on the front of a verb can mark tense or emphasis: سَ “will”, قَدْ “already/surely”. On a noun, الْ means “the”.

words.english: has (with past tense); surely (with present tense)

words.note: Attaches to the front of a present-tense verb. سَيَعْلَمُ = he will know.
Attaches to the front of a word for emphasis. لَهُوَ = indeed he.
Attaches to a verb to make a command: “let him do…”.
Attaches to the front of a noun. الْكِتَاب = the book.
The ّ matters. إِنَّ = indeed (it highlights what follows). إِنْ = if. Same idea with أَنَّ (that) vs أَنْ (to / that).
An extra ا at the start of a describing word often means more or most. كَبِير big, أَكْبَر bigger.

words.arabic: آدَم، نُوح، إِبْرَاهِيم، لُوط، إِسْمَاعِيل، إِسْحَاق، يَعْقُوب، إِسْرَائِيل، يُوسُف، هُود، شُعَيْب، صَالِح، مُوسَى، عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَم
words.english: Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Lut, Isma'eel, Ishaq, Ya'qub, Isra'eel, Yusuf, Hud, Shu'ayb, Salih, Musa, 'Isa ibnu Maryam

words.note: A ة at the end often marks a feminine word, or one of something. آيَة = a sign, لَيْلَة = a night.
Each verb is shown as “he did” it. Hunt for the same three letters in other shapes: يَفْعَلُ he does, فَعَلُوا they did.

words.english: to raise, to resurrect, to send
to make, to place, to set up
to be grateful, to give thanks
to be true, to say the truth
to bear witness, to be present, to testify

words.note: When the last two of the three letters are the same, they often squeeze into one with a ّ. رَدَّ (he returned) is ر + د + د.

words.english: to go astray, to err, to lose

words.note: Some verbs start with و that disappears in other shapes. وَعَدَ he promised, يَعِدُ he promises — same word, with the و gone.

words.english: to put, to set, to give birth
to befall, to fall, to fulfil
to describe, to ascribe, to attribute

words.note: Some verbs have a middle و or ي that shows up as ا. قَالَ he said, يَقُولُ he says, قُلْ say — all the same word.

words.english: to be close to, to almost do

words.note: Some verbs end in ى, و, or ي that can shorten or drop. هَدَى he guided, يَهْدِي he guides, اهْدِنَا guide us.

words.english: to forgive, to excuse, to forgo
to decree, to fulfil, to judge
to be satisfied, to be content, to be pleased
to be safe, to feel safe, to trust

words.note: Doubling the middle letter often means doing the action to someone. عَلِمَ he knew, عَلَّمَ he taught. Look for that ّ.

words.english: to adorn, to make something seem fair
to accept as true, to pronounce to be true
to accuse of falsehood, to deny

words.note: An extra ا after the first letter often means the action involves someone else. قَتَلَ he killed, قَاتَلَ he fought.

words.english: to declare, to apprise, to inform
to call out, to cry unto

words.note: An extra أ at the start often means causing the action. خَرَجَ he went out, أَخْرَجَ he brought out.

words.english: to do good, to do excellently
to bring forth, to drive out
to send back, to take back
to reform, to improve, to make peace
to make lawful, to cause to dwell
to leave in error, to send astray
to cast, to throw, to place
to rescue, to save, to deliver
to give trouble, to harm, to annoy

words.note: A تـ at the start often means the action happens in you, or by yourself. تَفَكَّرَ he reflected — the thinking is happening inside.

words.english: to turn away, to take for friend
to make somebody die, to receive in full
to be blessed, to be exalted

words.note: A ت after the first letter is extra — it often means taking the action on. اِتَّبَعَ he followed, اِتَّقَى he guarded himself.

words.english: to fear (God), to be on guard
to be rightly guided, to find the right path, to follow the right path

words.note: Letters استـ at the start often mean seeking that action. غَفَرَ he forgave, اسْتَغْفَرَ he asked forgiveness.

words.english: to be straight, to act straight
one who associates partners with Allah
to follow, to cause to follow
